Drops OtpCodes, RentalDetails, SaleDetails, ServiceReviewDocuments tables and Properties.PriceCurrencyId column. Already applied to production. Down() recreates the tables, but any data present between the drop and a restore is lost; do not run Down in production without a fresh pre-migration backup.
Raw SQL: CREATE EXTENSION btree_gist plus an exclusion constraint on UnitBookingRanges; forward-fix, do not restore over newer booking data.
Finding F2. New nullable-default-false column plus a filtered index; application rollback may leave the column unused.

Finding F3. Raw SQL: a guarded pre-check (RAISE EXCEPTION, no row modified) refuses to apply if a case-variant duplicate email already exists, then creates IX_Users_Email_Lower on lower(Email). Forward-fix (resolve the duplicate, re-run); the pre-existing case-sensitive IX_Users_Email is left in place, so Down only drops the new index.

Finding F4. Five CHECK constraints on Properties (Area/Rooms/ColdRent/WarmRent/PurchasePrice), each `col IS NULL OR col > 0` -- no column type/nullability change. Fails atomically (no row modified) if an existing row already violates one; run scripts/database/audit-f4-numeric-constraints.sql first. Down drops the constraints.
Finding F7. Two new nullable columns plus a filtered index for the account-deletion delay-window sweep; application rollback may leave them unused.

Index-only (pg_trgm GIN on Properties.Title/Description for the ILIKE keyword search). No data change; if a query-plan or write-latency regression appears, drop the two indexes (concurrently) and forward-fix.

Makes ShortStayListings.Latitude/Longitude nullable and, via raw SQL, nulls out the (0,0) placeholder pin every listing got before the create form had location fields. Down restores NOT NULL with a 0,0 default, which would re-introduce that meaningless placeholder on the rows this migration just cleaned up; forward-fix, do not run Down in production.

STG-001/002 data repair. Raw SQL sets IsMain=false only on PropertyImages rows that are already soft-deleted (IsDeleted=true); no schema change, live rows untouched. Down is a no-op because the old IsMain value of a deleted image carries no meaning; forward-fix, no restore needed.

QA Phase 7. Adds Properties.ClosedAt/ImagesCompactedAt (nullable) and the stored generated column Properties.SearchText, which makes PostgreSQL rewrite the Properties table once under an exclusive lock (a few seconds at the current size; apply in a quiet minute), plus a filtered index and a pg_trgm GIN index created with raw SQL. No existing value is changed. Application rollback is safe (the old code ignores the new columns); Down drops the columns and indexes and loses only ClosedAt/ImagesCompactedAt, which can be rebuilt from Status and UpdatedAt of Sold/Rented rows. Forward-fix preferred.

Data only, no schema change. Sets the rate of USD (1), EUR (0.8922) and SYP (13400) and activates them, creating the rows if missing; other currencies are untouched. It overwrites rates an administrator set earlier, once. Down is a no-op because the previous values were placeholders; to change a rate afterwards use PUT /api/admin/currencies/{code}, no restore needed.

Additive tables/columns plus two raw-SQL backfills on ServiceProviders (Status from IsActive, ApprovedCategories from existing offerings); both are idempotent and only touch the new columns. Forward-fix; Down drops only what Up added.

Data only, no schema change. Sets the Syrian pound rate to 134 per dollar (redenominated scale) only while the stored rate is still above 1000, so a rate an administrator already set on the new scale is kept. Down is a no-op because the old-scale value was wrong for this product; to change the rate afterwards use PUT /api/admin/currencies/SYP, no restore needed.
Backward-compatible expansion: three nullable columns and a filtered index on Properties; application rollback leaves them unused.

Additive columns and one table plus one raw-SQL backfill on ServiceRequests (ConfirmedAt = CreatedAt, LastActivityAt = UpdatedAt for existing rows); idempotent and touches only the new columns. Application rollback is safe (the old code ignores the new columns, and the old app is served by the API's no-intent path); Down drops only what Up added and loses only the conversation messages and stamps, which cannot be rebuilt. Forward-fix preferred.
Backward-compatible expansion: a Priority column with a default, a nullable DedupeKey and a filtered unique index on Notifications; application rollback leaves them unused.
Backward-compatible expansion: one new table (NotificationPreferences) keyed by user; application rollback leaves it unused.
Backward-compatible expansion: three nullable columns and a filtered index on ShortStayListings; application rollback leaves them unused.

No data is changed. Raw SQL only adds 18 foreign keys and 11 CHECK constraints as NOT VALID and then validates each one inside its own sub-transaction: if existing rows break a rule the migration still succeeds, the constraint stays NOT VALID (still enforced for new or changed rows) and a WARNING names it; scripts/database/normalize-schema-integrity-check.sql lists the rows. It also drops 25 indexes that are exact left prefixes of another index on the same table (no data, rebuildable). Down drops the new constraints and indexes and recreates the dropped ones; the schema after Down was verified identical to the previous migration. Application rollback is safe: the old code never relied on the missing keys and every dropped index is covered by a wider one. Forward-fix preferred.

Schema only on PhoneOtpChallenges: widens NormalizedPhoneNumber from 16 to 1024 characters (the number is now stored encrypted), adds the nullable PhoneNumberLookupHash column and moves the send-rate index to it. Existing rows keep their values. Down drops the new column and index, deletes only the challenges whose number is encrypted (longer than 16; challenges live five minutes) and shrinks the column back. The clear-text copies on Users are not touched by this migration: they are removed by the explicit phone lookup backfill after deploy, and PhonePlaintext:Mode=Restore writes them back before an API rollback. Forward-fix preferred.

Launch audit A2-002/A3-002. Raw SQL cancels duplicate open visit requests (Status 0/5), keeping the oldest per property and requester, then adds a filtered unique index; the PropertyReviews unique index becomes filtered to live rows. Application rollback is safe. Down cannot rebuild the unfiltered review index once a user rewrote a deleted review, so forward-fix; cancelled duplicates are not restored (they were never meant to exist).
